Resolve chromosome-level gains against depth and nested calls

Source: R/caller.R
resolve_nested.Rd

A diluted sub-chromosomal imbalance (a 1p loss, a distal CN-LOH) makes the whole chromosome look like a 2:1 gain: at chromosome scale the allelic term of the nested event dominates while its depth contrast is diluted, and the gain state (f 2/3) fits a diluted haplotype fraction better than 1:0 / 2:0. Per cell, a reportable gain call of a classes region therefore needs

  1. depth support: the gain depth LLR of the row itself is positive (dl_gain > min_dl_gain; for the Student-t null, z above the midpoint between neutral and the gain shift), so the allelic term alone cannot carry a gain label; and

  2. (class chrom) no nested explanation: no called loss / CN-LOH row of the same cell and chromosome in nested classes (arm, 50 Mb, 20 Mb) with a higher score. A gain failing either rule stays in the table with called = TRUE but reportable = FALSE and resolved naming the reason (no_depth, nested <region> <state>). With promote, the best (highest-score) nested loss / CN-LOH call that explains a dropped chromosome gain is made reportable (resolved = "replaces <region> gain"; arm and 50 Mb losses are reportable anyway, a 20 Mb one is promoted).

Usage

resolve_nested(
  calls,
  scores = NULL,
  min_dl_gain = 0,
  classes = c("chrom", "event"),
  nested = c("arm", "50Mb", "20Mb"),
  promote = TRUE
)

Arguments

calls

cell-level calls table (call_table())

scores

scored rows (cell, region, dl_gain); NULL when calls has dl_gain

min_dl_gain

minimal gain depth LLR of a reportable gain

classes

classes whose reportable gains need depth support

nested

classes of the nested calls that can explain a chromosome gain

promote

make the explaining nested call reportable

Value

calls with column resolved (NA = unchanged) and updated reportable
